A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same coalition-attribution work. All pages, equations and Figure 1 are readable. v1 ends after the references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A and B, which were inspected.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical attribution relationships and illustrative image and sentence examples, without original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical presentation. Its new appendices contain mathematical derivations, not empirical results.

M1.justification: The AND/OR interaction decomposition and proposed coalition attribution in Equation 6 are unchanged. The added proofs do not alter the attribution procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks. The image, tokenization and sentiment examples remain the same conceptual illustrations.

E2.justification: Shapley and Banzhaf values remain the same theoretical reference methods. Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The existing masking and model-output definitions are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests or empirical case studies are added or removed. The new appendices prove existing theoretical statements.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The illustrative allocation coefficients and stated attribution relationships are unchanged. v2 adds derivations supporting existing results, without new empirical scores or findings.

T1.justification: v1 states Theorems 2 and 3 with explanatory prose; v2 adds Appendices A and B deriving the Shapley and Banzhaf interaction-allocation formulas. These substantially expand the formal arguments, while existing definitions, theorem statements and coalition axioms remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an interaction-based Shapley reformulation, its extension to coalition attribution, and an explanation of attribution conflicts through interactions involving partial coalitions. Abstract corrections preserve these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretation of partial-coalition interactions as the source of attribution conflicts is retained, together with the argument for explaining rather than forcibly eliminating those conflicts. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The existing technical description is retained. v2 adds no implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware information or code/data access information; its added detail consists of mathematical proofs.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Shapley, Banzhaf and prior AND/OR interaction research are unchanged. The appendices introduce no identifiable new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 repairs garbled abstract wording and spelling, adds Bo Fan to the author list, and appends two proof sections. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block changes from a compact shared listing to separate blocks, causing text and equation reflow. The appendices add displayed derivations. Figure 1 and its caption are unchanged, and neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: The new derivations make the reasoning behind Theorems 2 and 3 more inspectable, and the abstract is clearer. However, Appendix A switches inconsistently between empty and nonempty intersection conditions in its OR-interaction derivation and contains an unresolved '?' reference for a combinatorial identity. These defects limit the improvement in theoretical support.
